approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, scored molecules. It samples breeding parents from high-scoring bands of a bounded population, combines connected fragments, and applies ordinary local mutations and short mutation walks. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchanges are already disabled. Stable canonical identity checks admit a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity to predict that pool jointly. Each batch position chooses the remaining maximizer of a fresh correlated score draw; accepted offspring then update both the prediction archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove only cross-candidate residual correlation from allocation, giving each candidate an independent Gaussian excursion with its existing jittered marginal variance. The fitted joint model and nonzero random exploration remain. No completed sibling of this current baseline is supplied. An earlier correlation-only control changed decisions but left one task unfinished, and its Parent still allowed direct aromatic exchanges. This experiment reuses that precise control on the exchange-free Parent and seeks a complete comparison under the current profile. It tests whether the search can avoid a material endpoint loss when dependence is removed; it adds neither a new acquisition objective nor a chemical diversity rule.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting uncertainty is the Parent n-62daf219c70a sharing allocation residuals across alternatives through its full conditional covariance without a complete component contrast establishing whether that dependence helps its current exchange-free search. Its actual three summary.json and run.log pairs show a complete panel: macro mean 0.5956696497334577, population SD 0.02659287062806747, and seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. Its indexed full audit reconstructs correlated selection in all 435 batches, each with nonzero fitted off-diagonal covariance; 3755 emitted positions differ from the available posterior-mean maximum. Those departures establish residual influence, not correlation contribution. Source and trajectories reproduce n-c55c3d520a2c, so the baseline adds a current comparator rather than independent trajectories or a component effect. The closest controlled removal, n-ae9cc6c2ca09 above the exchange-containing count-posterior Parent n-559d25e9c9c7, preserves jittered marginals and changes 411 of 426 same-pool batch sets in its recorded audit. Its actual deco_hop seed-0 summary is buggy after 210 evaluations, with no final macro score. Its paired gain 0.012738055065837972 over only two complete seeds cannot resolve contribution. Selected-pair absolute model correlation increased and same-pool nonempty-core coverage decreased, so independent noise did not demonstrate chemical diversification. The broader mean-only removal n-852bc7be4d7c lost 0.040407162268268314 against that historical Parent; it motivates preserving marginal residual influence here, not an answer about the new Parent. This is unresolved dependence contribution, not demonstrated harmful covariance or a diagnosed factorization failure.
hypothesis: Remove cross-candidate dependence from allocation residual draws by sampling independent Gaussian residuals with the Parent's unchanged jittered marginal variances, while retaining the fitted count-based joint posterior.

finding_summary.headline: Correlation removal executes correctly but lowers the complete matched mean by 0.018447
finding_summary.insights: The isolated reverse control supports a positive contribution of correlated allocation residuals in the current exchange-free search, with substantial seed and task dependence. Independent draws do not guarantee diverse selections: on the same Child pools they raise mean absolute fitted-model correlation from 0.05063 to 0.05465 and slightly reduce nonempty typed and generic core counts. Strict local parent beats increase from 629 to 661 and incumbent gains from 258 to 273, yet the endpoint mean falls, so these local measures do not explain the benefit. Molecular evidence preserves compact conventional alternatives and some larger improving families alongside reactive bond environments, repeated large assemblies and destructive fragments; no single chemistry or size rule accounts for the score. Which adaptive choices mediate the benefit remains open. The earlier correlation-removal panel still lacks its timed-out seed-0 endpoint, and its two-seed gain under a different Parent and profile remains separate evidence. This complete comparison answers the current component question without repairing or reinterpreting that historical record.
finding_summary.results: All 435 allocations remove analytic residual cross-covariance while preserving the original jittered marginal variances. Every sampled value and selected identity reconstructs. Replaying correlated draws on the same Child inputs changes 422 of 435 selected sets; thirteen sets coincide, and residuals still move 3,747 of 4,350 choices away from the available mean maximum. Mean final score falls from 0.595670 to 0.577222, a paired loss of 0.018447 against the registered 0.002 scale. The no-material-loss prediction is therefore contradicted, although the removal itself is confirmed. Seed macro changes are -0.066439, +0.035503 and -0.024407: ten task-seed endpoints fall and five rise. The strongest loss is deco_hop seed 0 (-0.253234); the strongest gain is sitagliptin_mpo seed 1 (+0.158750). All tasks complete under the matched profile.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, aryl amines and crowded nitrogen rings coexist with large repeated assemblies and reactive difluoroamino groups
molecular.overall_character: This report concerns the fresh complete panel for n-54adc6a641e8. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were present and read. Each task has 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2; no task lacks trajectories. The brief reports complete Child evaluation and complete current-profile pairing with code Parent n-62daf219c70a, with no profile-mismatched seeds. Chemistry comparisons below use those published Parent trajectories, not an older incomplete correlation experiment. The report does not decide activation, rank algorithms or attribute a chemical change to residual correlation. The output is ring-rich and largely aromatic: ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9586 to 0.9828 and aromatic-string incidence 0.9552 to 0.9736. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts, aromatic-atom fractions or proof of geometric aromaticity. Families include compact benzofused azaaromatic amides, substituted indole/amidine systems, linked nitrogen/oxygen carbonyl heterocycles, flexible and bridged aryl amines, crowded nitrogen-dicarbonyl rings and fluorinated nitrogen-rich heterocycles. Some trajectories also produce very large repeated carbonyl/aryl assemblies and small poor-scoring fragments. Families differ across seeds, but within-seed leaders often remain close relatives, supporting moderate overall diversity. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug-likeness weak. Reactive N-halogen, peroxide, O-F, imino-fluoride and thioaldehyde environments coexist with recognizable amides, carbonyls, amines and ethers. The strongest fluorinated family has two difluoroaminomethyl groups, with fluorines attached to nitrogen; those are not ordinary fluoromethyl substituents. Its lack of cumulated double bonds removes one specific Parent concern without establishing a chemically stable molecule. Counterexamples to uniform chemical failure include a high-scoring N-hydroxy azaaromatic amide and a comparatively conventional flexible aryl tertiary amine. Other gains involve larger or more crowded rings, so higher score is not synonymous with better synthetic plausibility. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 for every task despite visible protonatable amines and potential stereogenic centres. Sizes below count heavy-atom tokens in cited trajectory SMILES; no synthesis, physical-property or conformational validation was performed. The digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, not each seed's best retained molecule. Parent comparisons rely on its published trajectories; cited_smiles contains only current molecules authorized by the digest or trusted current trajectory list.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 25 heavy atoms: an ethyl/dimethyl-substituted benzofused azaaromatic ring linked through an N-chloro amide to a chloropyridyl ring. A nearby leader uses N-hydroxy amide chemistry and an additional carbon-bound chlorine. Seed 2 retains a 25-heavy-atom methoxy/methyl indole-like amidine family with halogen substitution on both ring and linker nitrogen. Seed 0 instead reaches a 25-heavy-atom partly dearomatized, expanded unsaturated N-fluorinated ring system attached to a fluoropyridyl imine. Mean proposal SMILES length is 43.2, with halogen incidence 0.9678. Compact aromatic and carbonyl/imine organization is plentiful, but reactive nitrogen substitution and atypical unsaturation remain prominent.
liabilities: N-Cl amides, N-F ring nitrogens and N-halogen amidines differ chemically from ordinary carbon-bound halogens.
The N-hydroxy amide is recognizable chemistry but does not validate every neighbouring N-halogen variant; the partly dearomatized unsaturated structures require separate assessment.
Late small fragments can lose the combined ring/linker context while retaining an imine or halogen.
missing_features: Conventional local alternatives preserving the favorable azaaromatic/linker arrangement are not consistently established at the leading score; the near-leading N-hydroxy amide is a counterexample to obligatory N-chlorination.
The expanded unsaturated and N-halogenated families lack demonstrated stable geometry, configuration and synthesis.
The observed gradients do not identify an absent exact target pharmacophore, and additional rings, nitrogen or halogens are not a general inferred solution.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 46 heavy atoms and combines linked heteroaromatic/carbonyl regions with branched fluorinated ether/acetal groups, an imidate-like connection, a carbon-linked nitrile and an O-linked cyanate. The large seed-0 leader contains peroxide, direct O-F and N-Cl environments alongside repeated diones and conjugated chains.
Dense short ring closures and extensive annulation may satisfy graph notation without demonstrating a stable aromatic or three-dimensional geometry.
missing_features: Stable independent arrangements preserving the favorable combined heterocyclic features are not consistently represented across seeds; very large repeated assemblies do not recover the stronger compact Parent organization.
The short aromatic-labelled ring closures, imidate-like linkages and highly substituted acetal centres lack demonstrated accessible geometry and chemical stability.
Conventional alternatives to cyanate, peroxide and heteroatom-halogen functionality are not established at comparable scores; the data do not identify one required target decoration.

The seed-1 leader reaches 0.633657779658626, while two related decorated molecules score 0.630172470325923 and 0.6302100372963424. These close values associate useful reward with a retained combined organization despite peripheral and connectivity changes. The Child seed-1 score exceeds Parent 0.6248206599713055, even though the leader is larger than the Parent's 32-heavy-atom example. per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 28 heavy atoms: an aminoethyl/fluorophenyl region linked through a benzylic bromide-containing chain to a densely bridged tertiary amine and aryl ether cage. Seed 0 instead reaches a 30-heavy-atom flexible aryl tertiary amine with phenol, methoxy, aniline and carbon-bound chlorines; its local functional groups are comparatively conventional. Seed 2 reaches a 33-heavy-atom polycyclic amine/aryl-ether structure with an azetidine-related region and an explicitly hydrogen-bearing, multiply substituted sulfur-oxo centre attached to nitrogen. That bracketed sulfur environment is not adequately described as an ordinary sulfoxide. Mean proposal SMILES length is 55.8 and halogen incidence 0.9885. Available aliphatic amines and aromatic regions are abundant; the main uncertainties concern bridges, local reactive groups and molecular identity.
liabilities: The strongest leader retains potentially reactive benzylic bromide and dense ring junctions, even though it avoids N-F and O-F.
The seed-2 hydrogen-bearing sulfur-oxo environment needs explicit chemical and valence-state assessment; its supplied representation does not establish an accessible compound.
The flexible aryl amine is a chemistry counterexample to uniformly implausible output, but its long hydrophobic chains and unassigned centres still lack property and identity validation.
missing_features: Stable local alternatives to benzylic bromide and the unusual sulfur environment retaining each leader's favorable aromatic/basic organization are not demonstrated at the same scores.
The bridged and substituted saturated centres lack explicit stereochemical and conformational identity; the flexible seed-0 leader shows that a crowded cage is not universally necessary.
Protonation states are not explicit in the neutral strings, but clear primary and tertiary amines are already present. Adding basic nitrogen without regard to context is not a supported diagnosis.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader has 36 heavy atoms and joins a propyl/ethoxy phenyl region to a densely bridged diaryl nitrogen-dicarbonyl assembly with N-methyl groups and adjacent N-N connections. Ring-bound unsaturation and potentially stereogenic junctions have no explicit assignments.
Small floor-scoring fragments still occur, while higher scores in the larger leaders prevent treating molecular growth itself as a universal defect.

Simpler independent connectivities preserving the favorable aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl presentation are not established at the leading scores.
The observations do not identify a missing exact target motif or justify universally increasing ring size or N-N content.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-54adc6a641e8 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task, with complete current-profile Parent n-62daf219c70a pairing. The bond-environment gap originally recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c persists in changed forms: current leaders contain N-Cl amides, repeated N(F)F groups, benzylic bromide, cyanate, peroxide, O-F, unusual sulfur-oxo and terminal thioaldehyde environments. Counterexamples include a near-leading N-hydroxy amide and a high-scoring flexible aryl tertiary amine with conventional carbon-bound chlorines. The concern is environment-specific, not an absence of ring systems, amides or basic centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently replace reactive local environments with conventional alternatives while retaining favorable molecular organization.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need chemically plausible local alternatives preserving feedback-supported functional relationships, and must distinguish carbon-bound fluorine from nitrogen-bound fluorine or direct O-F. Preserve the conventional examples as evidence that reactive bonds are not universal requirements. The current scores do not establish that a blanket filter improves reward or attribute any liability to residual-correlation handling.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-54adc6a641e8 under complete current-profile Search comparison with n-62daf219c70a, continuing the earlier context/coverage gap from n-c55c3d520a2c. An 80-heavy-atom repeated assembly remains below its matched 30-heavy-atom Parent leader, a 56-heavy-atom assembly scores extremely poorly, and tiny halogen or hydrocarbon fragments reach observed floors. Counterexamples include larger linked and bridged families that exceed some matched Parent endpoints; a smaller final relative of the 80-heavy-atom leader does not automatically score better. Distinct seed families remain, so this is not global scaffold collapse.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful functional-group context while limiting repeated elaboration and destructive fragmentation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback should test independent connectivities and simplifications that preserve useful aromatic, carbonyl and basic/polar relationships, rather than treating repeated motifs or reduced atom count as sufficient. The evidence supports control of chemical context and exploration of plausible alternatives, not a fixed size threshold or universal penalty on molecular growth. Chemistry association does not identify which search component caused the observed coverage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-54adc6a641e8 across the supplied complete Search panel and Parent comparison. Current leaders contain extra short closures in an aromatic-labelled fragment, dense amine and dicarbonyl bridges, and a small unsaturated nitrogen ring. The Parent geometric concern originated in n-c55c3d520a2c, but an entire current proposal set has cumulated-double-bond-string incidence 0.0 while yielding high-scoring fluorinated leaders. A flexible aryl tertiary amine and an aromatic near-relative of the hydroxylated cyclic leader are further counterexamples to a need for every difficult topology.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently establish credible geometry for short aromatic-labelled ring closures, crowded bridges and small unsaturated heterocycles.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need geometry-sensitive assessment of connectivity, unsaturation and conformational accessibility, together with alternatives retaining learned favorable arrangements. Aromatic notation and ring digits cannot certify a realizable structure. The evidence does not support banning all small or bridged rings, assuming the Parent's specific strained motif persists, or claiming that geometry filtering must improve score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-54adc6a641e8 on all supplied Search Seeds at 300 observations per task, continuing the identity gap recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a. Every task has stereocentre-string and formal-charge-string incidence 0.0, despite substituted saturated rings, bridged amine frameworks, fluorinated centres and imine/enol-like functions. Obvious primary and tertiary amines remain present; neutral strings do not establish a lack of protonatable chemistry. Achiral or configurationally labile examples should be distinguished from those requiring stable stereoisomer assignment.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves relevant stereochemical and molecular-state identity unspecified in saturated, bridged and tautomer-sensitive structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations need to preserve or explicitly resolve relevant stereochemistry, with separate treatment of protonation, tautomerism and imine/alkene configuration. Do not infer biological activity, accessibility or a score penalty from unspecified state alone. These observations establish incomplete chemical identity, not a component-specific causal result or proof that adding charge or enumeration raises reward.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Accepted-only task-local archive, bounded greedy survivor population and score-quantile breeding selection.
Connected-fragment crossover, optional post-crossover mutation and ordinary one-/two-/three-call continuation with bounded retries and saturation rules.
All seven ordinary atom/bond/ring mutation families, fixed weights/atom bounds and disabled direct aromatic C/N exchange with passive opportunity tracing.
Sanitization, stable canonical isomeric identity and original-graph provenance, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, fixed surplus pools and announced batches.
Shared count-Morgan features and canonical cache, generalized Tanimoto GP, accepted-data normalization, fixed observation noise, full latent covariance and full jittered Cholesky.

Nonzero Gaussian marginal residual influence, original random-array call and task-local generator, stable masked selection, identity-bound predictions and next-fit probes; cross-candidate allocation residual correlation is removed.

Fresh objective-local state, prepared CONFIG and prescribed resources/budget, finite guards and first-valid-pool numerical fallback; later jitter and recovery branches remain source-preserved but unexercised.
